storyline: Judge calibration for memory-QA verdicts — docs/testing-strategy.md §7.6 open item 'judge calibration for every graded number' (§10 item L). Every published memory benchmark (LoCoMo's J, LongMemEval, Letta's leaderboard) leans on an LLM judge; the 2026 audit literature (MemStrata arXiv 2610.05343 — 1.5-2.3% same-seed label flips; 'Auditing Long-Term Memory Evaluation' arXiv 2609.38021) shows uncalibrated judges are the weak link. This suite measures OUR judge protocol (Mem0-style binary CORRECT/WRONG, question -> gold -> hypothesis, temperature 0) against 24 gold-labeled items in six classes: correct-gold, correct-paraphrase, wrong-number, wrong-entity, partial (the leniency profile — no gold label, recorded), abstention-on-answerable (must be WRONG) and abstention-on-unanswerable (must be CORRECT, the LongMemEval _abs contract). Also measured: run-to-run flip rate (3 judge runs per item at temperature 0) and order sensitivity (reference-after-candidate vs reference-before, 6-item probe). Model: the judge and the agent are the same served model (agnes-3.0-flash) — the honest constraint of a metered single-model deployment, recorded in every receipt.

judgeProtocol.system: You are a strict grader for question-answering against a reference answer. Compare the candidate answer to the reference answer for factual equivalence: the candidate must convey the same fact(s) — exact wording is not required, but a wrong number, wrong entity, missing required detail, or a refusal when the reference contains the answer is WRONG. Answer with exactly one word: CORRECT or WRONG.
